title: Centre Fuselage Lower Shell — External Repair Patch on the Outer Skin

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: External repair patch applied to the outer skin of the centre fuselage lower shell, restoring the section after skin damage without entering the compartment behind it.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the outer skin of the centre fuselage lower shell by an external patch, so that the section can be recovered without disturbing the equipment installations behind the skin.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the damage from outside and confirm it from inside before choosing this scheme. The external patch is the right answer when the compartment behind the skin is full and emptying it would cost more than the patch, which on this part of the shell is usually the case. Measure the damage in two axes and check the frame and stringer positions against the drawing; a patch that crosses a frame needs the frame-crossing detail on sheet 2 and cannot be done to sheet 1. Confirm that no existing repair lies within one hundred millimetres, because two patches that close on each other have never been substantiated as a pair.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Establish the damage boundary from outside and mark it. 2. Confirm from inside the compartment that no equipment attachment falls inside the patch footprint. 3. Trim the damage to a smooth rectangle with radiused corners to the minimum radius on the drawing. 4. Prepare the surface and pass the water break test. 5. Cut the patch from the sheet stock to the size on the drawing, with the grain direction as marked. 6. Drill the patch pattern with the jig, working from the centre outwards, and de-burr every hole. 7. Do an eddy current inspection of every hole in the parent skin. 8. Where the patch crosses a frame, install the angle D5322115000135 and the cleat D5322118609777 to the frame-crossing detail. 9. Install the splice plate PEL735035-02 where the drawing calls for a load path across the trim. 10. Install the fasteners wet with sealant in the marked sequence, in two passes. 11. Where a blind position occurs, use the blind rivet EN172060-68 in accordance with the drawing note. 12. Seal the patch edge all round with a fillet and feather the protective scheme into the surrounding paint. 13. Record the patch position against the frame and stringer grid.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection of the patch perimeter fastener row at installation and record it. Repeat the eddy current inspection of the perimeter row every four thousand flight cycles for the life of the repair. Do a detailed visual inspection of the sealant fillet and of the paint feather at every scheduled structural check; water tracking under the patch edge is the failure mode that ends this repair. Record the patch position on the aircraft repair map so that any later internal work in the same bay can be assessed against it.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Trimmed damage up to 150 mm by 150 mm on sheet 1, or up to 250 mm by 150 mm crossing not more than one frame on sheet 2. Not within 100 mm of an existing repair and not across a stringer run-out.

repair_drawings.title: External patch, centre fuselage lower shell, plain and frame-crossing details

type_data.fastener_pattern: Three rows, 20 mm pitch, 15 mm edge distance, staggered; blind rivets only at the positions marked on the drawing
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The patch is life-limited to 16 000 flight cycles with a repeat eddy current inspection of the perimeter row every 4 000 flight cycles. A second patch within 100 mm is not permitted and requires an engineering assessment.
